subject: english-language
title: Communities of Practice
welcome_lead: Beyond crude social class, Eckert's high-school ethnography revealed identity-driven variation. Welcome to the lunch-table.
meta_desc: Eckert's communities of practice, jocks and burnouts, and third-wave sociolinguistics at A-Level.
final_note: You have moved beyond class-as-label into identity-as-practice — variation is something speakers do, not just have.

concepts.def: A group united by shared activity and practice (Eckert & McConnell-Ginet 1992) — more dynamic than fixed social class.

Approach (Eckert 2012) focused on style, identity construction and indexicality rather than fixed correlations.
The way linguistic features point to (index) social identities and stances.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Eckert spent two years in a Detroit high school. She found two emergent groups — jocks (school-oriented, future-bound) and burnouts (urban, working-class trajectory).

The burnouts led the Northern Cities Vowel Shift, with girls in particular pushing the change. Identity within a community of practice predicted variation better than parental occupation.

Giles's Communication Accommodation Theory describes convergence (sounding more like the addressee to gain approval) and divergence (sounding less alike to mark identity).

A call-centre worker softening regional features illustrates upward convergence; a teenager exaggerating slang to mark distance illustrates divergence.
Eckert's 2012 article on three waves argues that variation is not just a social symptom but an active resource speakers use to project stance and identity moment to moment.

mcqs.q: Penelope Eckert's high school study identified which two groups?
options: Jocks and burnouts
Mods and rockers
Goths and preps
Nerds and athletes

mcqs.q: Communication Accommodation Theory was developed by:
options: Howard Giles
William Labov
Robin Lakoff
David Crystal

mcqs.q: What does Labov's research show about language variation?
options: Language varies systematically by social class, gender, age and context — and speakers shift style depending on formality, often unconsciously.
Labov showed that everyone speaks the same way regardless of background.
Convergence means two languages merge into one new language.
Labov showed that working-class people speak ungrammatically.

mcqs.q: What is convergence in accommodation theory?
options: Overt prestige is loud speech and covert prestige is quiet speech.
Convergence means two languages merge into one new language.
When a speaker adjusts their speech to be more similar to their interlocutor's — to express solidarity, gain approval or ease communication.
Convergence is when two speakers start using identical accents permanently.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between overt and covert prestige?
options: Overt prestige is the high status of standard varieties recognised by society (RP, Standard English); covert prestige is the hidden status of non-standard varieties within particular groups, signalling solidarity or toughness.
Only standard language has prestige; non-standard varieties have none.
Labov showed that everyone speaks the same way regardless of background.
Overt prestige is loud speech and covert prestige is quiet speech.
